fixtures.question: What was the final outcome and winner of the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
fixtures.ground_truth:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup concluded on July 19, 2026, with Spain emerging as the champion, defeating Argentina 1-0 in extra time. 

The final was held at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, and was attended by 80,663 spectators. The match remained goalless through 90 minutes of regular play and went into extra time. Spain scored the winning goal in the 106th minute, scored by Ferran Torres.

Spain's victory marked their second World Cup title, their first being in 2010. Spain also became the first nation to hold both the men's and women's World Cup titles simultaneously, as the Spanish women's team had won the FIFA Women's World Cup in 2023.

Argentina, the defending champions, were unable to secure a second consecutive title. They struggled throughout the match, particularly after Enzo Fernández was sent off in the 93rd minute, leaving them with ten players for the remainder of the match, including extra time. Argentina did not manage a single shot on target during the entire match, and goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez set a World Cup final record with 11 saves.

Spain's defensive performance was outstanding, conceding only one goal during the entire tournament, which was also the only goal in the final. Goalkeeper Unai Simón recorded seven clean sheets, the most by any goalkeeper in a single World Cup. Spain outshot Argentina 20-2 over the course of the 120 minutes. 

The final also featured the first-ever World Cup halftime show, which included performances by notable artists.
